searches.question: Can they search my phone?
searches.short_answer: They need a real reason to suspect YOU broke a rule. Ask to call your parents first.
searches.explanation: Schools can't randomly grab phones. They need specific suspicion about you.
searches.script: Excuse me, I'd really prefer to call my parent or guardian before anything happens with my phone. I'm not trying to be difficult, but I know I have the right to have them involved.

searches.question: Can they search my locker?
searches.short_answer: Probably yes. Most schools own lockers.
searches.script: I understand the locker belongs to the school, but can you please tell me what this is about? I'd also like my parents to know this is happening.

searches.question: Can they go through my bag?
searches.short_answer: Only with specific suspicion about you, not random checks.
searches.script: I'd like to know what specific rule I'm suspected of breaking before you go through my bag. I'm not trying to cause trouble, but I want to make sure this is fair.

searches.question: Can they search my car?
searches.short_answer: If parked at school, usually yes - you agreed by parking there.
searches.script: Can you show me where in the parking policy it says you can search my car? I want to understand my rights here, and I'd like to call my parents.

searches.question: Can they strip search me?
searches.short_answer: Almost NEVER. Refuse and demand parents immediately.
searches.script: No, I do not agree to that. I want my parents contacted right now, and I'd like to speak with a lawyer. I know the Supreme Court has ruled against this kind of search.

searches.question: Can a teacher read my texts?
searches.short_answer: Not without good reason. Your phone is private.
searches.script: That's my personal phone with my private messages. I don't feel comfortable with that, and I'd like to call my parent before this goes any further.

searches.question: Can they make me empty my pockets?
searches.short_answer: They need reasonable suspicion first.
searches.script: I'd like to know the specific reason you're asking me to do this. I want to cooperate, but I also want to make sure my rights are being respected.

searches.question: Can they use metal detectors?
searches.short_answer: Yes, if everyone goes through them. Random selection is trickier.
searches.script: Is this a screening that everyone has to go through, or am I being singled out? I just want to understand what's happening.

searches.question: Can a school resource officer search me?
searches.short_answer: SROs are police - they usually need MORE reason than teachers.
searches.explanation: SROs are actual law enforcement and typically need probable cause.
searches.script: I understand you're a police officer, but I don't consent to being searched. I'd like my parents to be here, and I'm choosing to remain silent until they arrive.

searches.question: Can they search everyone's bags randomly?
searches.short_answer: Mass searches without individual suspicion are usually NOT okay.
searches.explanation: Schools need suspicion about a specific person, not a whole group.
searches.script: I notice you're searching everyone's bags, not just mine. I don't think a blanket search like this is allowed without a specific reason to suspect me individually.

discipline.question: I'm getting suspended. What now?
discipline.short_answer: You have the right to know charges and tell your side.
discipline.explanation: Short suspensions need basic due process.
discipline.script: I want to understand exactly what I'm being accused of. Can you put the specific charges in writing? I have the right to hear the accusations and tell my side of the story.

discipline.question: Can they expel me?
discipline.short_answer: Only after a formal hearing where you can defend yourself.
discipline.explanation: Expulsion is serious - you get a real hearing.
discipline.script: Before anything is decided, I want a formal hearing where I can present my side. I have the right to defend myself, and I'd like my parents there too.

discipline.question: Do I have to stay for detention?
discipline.short_answer: Usually yes, but parents should be notified.
discipline.script: I'll serve the detention, but I need you to let my parents know about this first so they can arrange transportation.

discipline.question: Others got lighter punishment. Fair?
discipline.short_answer: Should be consistent. If it's about race/gender, that's discrimination.
discipline.explanation: Can't punish you harder because of who you are.
discipline.script: I've noticed that other students who did the same thing got a different punishment. Can we talk about why my consequence is different? I want to make sure this is being handled fairly.

discipline.question: Can I appeal?
discipline.script: I'd like to know exactly how the appeals process works. Can you give me that information in writing so my parents and I can go over it together?

discipline.question: Zero tolerance - any rights?
discipline.short_answer: Yes! You still get to explain what happened.
discipline.explanation: Zero tolerance doesn't mean zero rights.
discipline.script: I understand this is a zero-tolerance situation, but I still have the right to explain what actually happened. The circumstances really matter here.

discipline.question: They want me to sign something.
discipline.short_answer: Read it first. Take it home if needed.
discipline.explanation: Don't sign what you don't understand.
discipline.script: I appreciate you explaining this, but I'm not comfortable signing anything right now. I'd like to take this home so my parents can read it first.

discipline.question: Can they call the cops on me?
discipline.short_answer: For serious stuff, yes. Schools can involve police.
discipline.script: If you're going to involve the police, I want to make clear that I'm exercising my right to remain silent and I'd like a lawyer and my parents present before any questioning.

discipline.question: ISS vs OSS - what are my rights in each?
discipline.short_answer: ISS = less formal. OSS = out of school, needs more due process.
discipline.explanation: Out-of-school suspension is more serious and you have more rights.
discipline.script: Can you clarify whether this is in-school or out-of-school suspension? I want to understand what this means for my assignments and my record.

discipline.question: Can they punish me for something off campus?
discipline.short_answer: Only if it substantially disrupts school. Off-campus speech is mostly protected.
discipline.explanation: Mahanoy ruling limits school authority over off-campus behavior.
discipline.script: This happened completely outside of school, on my own time. I don't believe the school has authority over what I do off campus, based on the Supreme Court's Mahanoy ruling.

attendance.question: What if I'm late a lot?
attendance.short_answer: Usually warnings, then detention, then bigger problems.
attendance.script: I know I've been late a lot and I want to work on that. Can we talk about what's been going on and figure out a plan together? There are some real reasons this has been happening.

attendance.question: What's excused absence?
attendance.short_answer: Sickness, emergency, religious holiday, mental health (some states).
attendance.script: I was absent because of a legitimate reason. What paperwork do you need from me to make this excused? I want to make sure everything is documented properly.

attendance.question: Can I leave early?
attendance.short_answer: Yes with parent permission and signing out.
attendance.script: My parent called ahead to let you know I need to leave early today. Where do I go to sign out properly?

attendance.question: What's truancy?
attendance.short_answer: Too many unexcused absences. Can lead to court.
attendance.script: I know my absences have added up, and I'm worried about the truancy thing. Can I talk to the counselor about what's going on and make a plan to get back on track?

attendance.question: Mental health day?
attendance.script: I'm really struggling with my mental health right now and I need a day to take care of myself. I know some states recognize mental health days as excused absences — does ours?

attendance.question: Parent won't write note?
attendance.short_answer: Talk to counselor. There might be bigger issues.
attendance.script: I'm in a difficult situation at home and I can't always get a note from my parent. Can I talk to the counselor confidentially about what's going on?

attendance.question: Can parents be charged for my truancy?
attendance.short_answer: Some states do charge parents but must offer interventions first.
attendance.explanation: Most states require schools try interventions before legal steps.
attendance.script: I understand truancy is serious, but what interventions or support has the school offered before taking legal action? I believe you're supposed to try other things first.

attendance.question: Chronic illness keeping me absent - options?
attendance.short_answer: Get doctor documentation. Request homebound or virtual services.
attendance.explanation: Chronic illness has accommodations available under federal law.
attendance.script: I have a chronic medical condition that's causing me to miss school. I'd like to discuss setting up a 504 plan or homebound services so I don't fall behind.

attendance.question: Dropped from class for absences?
attendance.short_answer: Check policy. If you have disability/medical reason, accommodations apply.
attendance.explanation: Medical and disability exceptions usually exist.
attendance.script: I understand the absence policy, but my absences are medical. Are there accommodations or exceptions for students with documented health issues?

attendance.question: Can I switch to homeschool to avoid truancy?
attendance.short_answer: Legal in all states but you must follow your state's rules.
attendance.explanation: Each state has different homeschool requirements and filing deadlines.
attendance.script: My family is considering homeschooling. Can you help me understand what the requirements are in our state so we can do this properly?

expression.question: Do I have free speech?
expression.short_answer: Yes, but limited. Can't disrupt learning.
expression.explanation: Students have rights but with limits.
expression.script: I believe what I'm expressing is protected speech. I'm not being disruptive or threatening — I'm sharing my opinion, which I have a right to do even as a student.

expression.question: Can I protest?
expression.short_answer: You can express views but might get marked absent.
expression.explanation: Walkouts are protected but have consequences.
expression.script: I want to express my views on this issue. I understand there might be consequences like being marked absent, but I believe peaceful expression is my right.

expression.question: Trouble for social media?
expression.short_answer: Off-campus posts mostly protected now. Threats = trouble.
expression.script: This post was made on my own time, on my own device, away from school. The Supreme Court has ruled that schools generally can't punish students for off-campus speech.

expression.question: Political clothing?
expression.short_answer: Usually yes unless vulgar or causing disruption.
expression.script: Can you point to the specific dress code rule my clothing violates? I believe wearing clothing that expresses my political views is protected speech.

expression.question: Practice religion at school?
expression.short_answer: YES. You can pray and wear religious items.
expression.script: This is part of my personal religious practice, and I have every right to practice my faith at school as long as I'm not disrupting class.

expression.question: Can I start a controversial club?
expression.short_answer: If other clubs exist, yours should be treated equally.
expression.script: I'd like to start this club, and since the school allows other student clubs, I believe mine should be treated the same way regardless of the viewpoint.

expression.question: Can they ban my hairstyle as 'distracting'?
expression.short_answer: If it targets race/culture, that's discrimination. CROWN Act applies.
expression.explanation: Many states protect cultural and natural hairstyles from discrimination.
expression.script: I believe this hairstyle policy unfairly targets my cultural background. Many states have passed the CROWN Act to protect natural hairstyles from exactly this kind of policy.

expression.question: Can they censor the school newspaper?
expression.short_answer: Depends on state. Some states protect student press from censorship.
expression.explanation: Hazelwood allows some censorship but many states override it.
expression.script: As a student journalist, I believe our school newspaper has the right to cover this topic. Does our state have student press freedom protections?

expression.question: Can I hand out flyers at school?
expression.short_answer: Usually yes during non-class time if not disruptive.
expression.explanation: Schools can set time/place rules but can't ban viewpoints.
expression.script: I'd like to hand out these flyers during lunch. I'm being peaceful and not disrupting any classes. Can you tell me the proper time and place to do this?

expression.question: Punished for a TikTok about school?
expression.short_answer: Off-campus posts are mostly protected unless causing major disruption.
expression.explanation: 2021 Supreme Court case says schools can't punish most off-campus speech.
expression.script: This TikTok was made off campus, on my own time, with my own device. Based on the Mahanoy Supreme Court case, the school's ability to punish off-campus speech is very limited.

administration.question: Fight unfair grade?
administration.script: I respectfully disagree with this grade and I'd like to discuss it. Can you walk me through exactly how it was calculated? I have evidence I'd like you to consider.

administration.question: Teacher treats me unfairly?
administration.script: I've been having some issues with how I'm being treated in class, and I've been keeping notes. Could I talk to the counselor or an administrator about this?

administration.question: Report bullying?
administration.short_answer: Tell trusted adult. Schools must investigate.
administration.explanation: Schools are required to address bullying.
administration.script: I need to report a bullying situation that's been going on. I have details about what's been happening, and I know the school is required to investigate.

administration.question: IEP/504 not being followed?
administration.short_answer: They MUST follow it. It's law.
administration.script: My IEP specifically says I'm supposed to receive certain accommodations, and those aren't being provided right now. I need to request an IEP meeting to address this.

administration.question: See school counselor?
administration.short_answer: Yes. Urgent issues should be seen quickly.
administration.script: I'm going through a really tough time and I need to talk to someone. Is the school counselor available? This feels pretty urgent.

administration.question: Can I see my school records?
administration.short_answer: Yes! FERPA gives you or parents access to your records.
administration.explanation: Request in writing and they must respond within 45 days.
administration.script: Under FERPA, I have the right to see my education records. I'm putting this request in writing, and I understand the school has 45 days to provide them.

administration.question: Teacher said something inappropriate to me?
administration.short_answer: Report immediately. Schools must investigate staff misconduct.
administration.explanation: Inappropriate comments by staff are taken seriously.
administration.script: Something happened with a staff member that made me really uncomfortable. I need to report this to someone in charge because I don't think what happened was appropriate.

administration.question: Can I transfer to another school?
administration.short_answer: Usually yes. Process varies by district.
administration.explanation: Intra-district transfers and open enrollment options exist.
administration.script: I've been thinking about transferring schools. Can you help me understand the process and what paperwork I need?

administration.question: School won't release my transcript?
administration.short_answer: They can't withhold for most reasons. Many states prohibit holds for fees.
administration.script: I need my transcript released for a college application. I don't think it's legal to withhold it, and I'd like to get this taken care of as soon as possible.

administration.question: Staff physically restrained me?
administration.short_answer: Only legal in genuine emergencies. Never as punishment.
administration.explanation: Most states strictly limit physical restraint to imminent danger.
administration.script: I need to report that a staff member physically restrained me, and it wasn't an emergency situation. I believe that violates school policy and possibly state law.

personal.question: Take my phone all day?
personal.short_answer: Many schools do this. Check handbook.
personal.script: I understand the phone policy, but I need to know specifically when I'll get my phone back. My parents need to be able to reach me in case of emergency.

personal.question: Dress code fair?
personal.short_answer: Can't discriminate by gender, race, religion.
personal.script: I've noticed the dress code seems to be enforced differently for different students. Is this rule being applied equally to everyone, regardless of gender or background?

personal.question: Carry medication?
personal.short_answer: Usually needs paperwork. Emergency meds often allowed.
personal.script: I have a medical condition that requires me to carry medication. I have the proper paperwork from my doctor. What forms do I need to fill out?

personal.question: Hair rules?
personal.short_answer: Natural hairstyles protected in many states.
personal.script: I believe this hair policy might be discriminatory against my natural hair. Several states have passed laws specifically protecting cultural hairstyles.

personal.question: Bathroom access?
personal.short_answer: Overly restrictive policies can be challenged.
personal.script: I have a medical reason that I need regular bathroom access. Restricting this is affecting my health, and I'd like to discuss an accommodation.

personal.question: LGBTQ+ rights?
personal.short_answer: Can be out, form clubs, free from harassment.
personal.script: I'm asking that my correct name and pronouns be used. I know the district has a policy about this, and I have the right to be called by my name.

personal.question: Clear backpack policy - is that legal?
personal.short_answer: Yes. Schools have latitude on safety measures like clear bags.
personal.explanation: Safety policies are generally upheld by courts.
personal.script: I understand the clear backpack requirement is for safety. Are there any alternatives for carrying personal items I need to keep private?

personal.question: Period products and bathroom access?
personal.short_answer: Restricting access for periods may violate Title IX.
personal.explanation: Many states now require schools to provide free period products.
personal.script: I have a health need related to my period that I can't put off. Restricting bathroom access for this reason may actually violate Title IX.

personal.question: Forced to remove piercings?
personal.short_answer: Safety reasons (labs, sports) okay. General ban is more questionable.
personal.script: Can you explain whether this is a safety requirement or just an appearance preference? If it's not about safety, I'd like to understand why it's required.

personal.question: Won't use my preferred name/pronouns?
personal.short_answer: Many districts require using preferred names. Policies are evolving.
personal.script: I've asked to be called by my preferred name, and the district policy supports this. Using the wrong name consistently is hurtful and I'd like it to stop.

grades.question: Grade changed without telling me?
grades.short_answer: You should be notified of grade changes.
grades.script: I noticed my grade changed without any explanation. Can you tell me why it was changed and show me the specific breakdown? I should have been notified.

grades.question: Failed for attendance?
grades.short_answer: Usually allowed but check policy for exceptions.
grades.script: I know there's an attendance policy that can affect grades, but are there any exceptions for my situation? I'd like to appeal this if possible.

grades.question: Extra credit refused?
grades.short_answer: Teachers don't have to offer it.
grades.script: I understand you don't have to offer extra credit, but are there any other assignments or ways I could demonstrate that I've learned the material?

grades.question: Accused of cheating unfairly?
grades.short_answer: You should get to explain before punishment.
grades.script: I'm being accused of cheating, but I didn't cheat. I'd like the chance to explain what happened and show my work process before any punishment is given.

grades.question: Test accommodations denied?
grades.short_answer: If you have IEP/504, they must provide them.
grades.script: My IEP or 504 plan requires specific testing accommodations, and they weren't provided. This is a legal requirement, not optional, and I need this addressed.

grades.question: Group project partner didn't do work?
grades.short_answer: Talk to teacher early. Most will consider individual effort.
grades.explanation: Proactive communication with teacher is key.
grades.script: I want to let you know that my group partner hasn't been contributing to our project. I've been doing the work and I have records to show my individual contributions.

grades.question: Late work policy too strict?
grades.short_answer: Must be applied equally. Document if it's uneven.
grades.script: I'm confused about how the late work policy was applied to my assignment. Is this the same standard being used for everyone in the class?

grades.question: Transcript GPA is wrong?
grades.short_answer: Request correction. Schools must fix errors in records.
grades.script: I've calculated my GPA based on my grades and it doesn't match what's on my transcript. I'd like to request a review and correction under FERPA.

grades.question: Teacher lost my assignment?
grades.short_answer: If you can prove submission, request a regrade.
grades.explanation: Digital submissions with timestamps are your friend.
grades.script: I submitted this assignment on time and I have proof — here's the timestamp. The fact that it was lost shouldn't penalize me. Can I resubmit?

grades.question: Final grade lower than my math shows?
grades.short_answer: Ask for complete grade breakdown. Teachers must explain.
grades.explanation: You deserve transparency in how grades are calculated.
grades.script: My final grade seems lower than what my individual assignment grades add up to. Can you show me the complete breakdown so I can understand how it was calculated?

sports.question: Cut from team unfairly?
sports.short_answer: Coaches have discretion, but can't discriminate.
sports.script: I was surprised not to make the team. Could you share what the selection criteria were? I want to make sure the process was fair for everyone.

sports.question: Benched for no reason?
sports.short_answer: Coaches decide playing time. Unless it's discrimination.
sports.script: I'd really like to understand what I need to improve to get more playing time. Can we have a conversation about specific things I should work on?

sports.question: Forced to play injured?
sports.short_answer: Never required. Your health comes first.
sports.script: I'm injured right now and I don't feel safe playing. My health has to come first, and I'd rather get a doctor's clearance before I risk making it worse.

sports.question: Hazing on the team?
sports.short_answer: Illegal in most states. Report it.
sports.script: Something is happening on the team that I think counts as hazing. I need to report it because it's making me and other players uncomfortable and it might be illegal.

sports.question: Drug testing for sports?
sports.short_answer: Schools can require it for athletes.
sports.script: I understand there's drug testing for athletes. Can you explain exactly what the policy is and what happens with the results?

sports.question: Can't afford pay-to-play fees?
sports.short_answer: Waivers should be available. Can't exclude for inability to pay.
sports.explanation: Many districts offer fee waivers for low-income families.
sports.script: My family can't afford the pay-to-play fee right now. Is there a fee waiver or financial assistance program so I can still participate?

sports.question: Concussion protocol not followed?
sports.short_answer: All 50 states have concussion laws. Must be followed.
sports.explanation: Return-to-play laws exist in every state.
sports.script: I hit my head during the game and I think the concussion protocol wasn't properly followed. I need to see a doctor before I play again — that's required by state law.

sports.question: Coach verbally abusing players?
sports.short_answer: Verbal abuse isn't coaching. Report to athletic director.
sports.explanation: There's a line between tough coaching and abuse.
sports.script: The way Coach has been talking to us crosses a line from tough coaching into verbal abuse. I'm going to talk to my parents about reporting this to the athletic director.

sports.question: Transgender athlete policy questions?
sports.short_answer: Varies by state. Know your state's specific rules.
sports.script: I want to participate in sports and I want to understand exactly what the policy is in our state for athletes like me. Can you point me to the current rules?

sports.question: Practice in extreme heat?
sports.short_answer: Must follow heat safety. Your health comes first.
sports.explanation: Heat illness is preventable. Guidelines exist.
sports.script: It's dangerously hot outside and I need a water break. Heat safety guidelines require rest and hydration in these conditions.

special-ed.question: How do I get an IEP?
special-ed.short_answer: Request evaluation in writing. School must respond.
special-ed.explanation: You have the right to be evaluated.
special-ed.script: I'm putting in a written request for a special education evaluation. I understand the school is required to respond to this request within a specific timeframe.

special-ed.question: School won't evaluate me?
special-ed.short_answer: They must respond to requests. File complaint if ignored.
special-ed.script: I requested an evaluation on a specific date and haven't heard back. The school is legally required to respond. I need an update on where things stand.

special-ed.question: IEP not being followed?
special-ed.script: My IEP says I'm supposed to receive certain services, but I'm not getting them. I'd like to document this and request an IEP meeting to fix it.

special-ed.question: Want different services?
special-ed.short_answer: Request IEP meeting to discuss changes.
special-ed.script: I think my current services aren't meeting my needs. I'd like to request an IEP meeting to discuss changes and I have some suggestions to bring.

special-ed.question: Graduation requirements different?
special-ed.script: I want to understand all my options for graduation requirements given my IEP. Can we discuss what accommodations and modifications are available?

special-ed.question: IEP changed without telling me?
special-ed.short_answer: Illegal! Parents must participate in IEP decisions.
special-ed.script: I wasn't notified that my IEP was changed. My parents are supposed to be part of every IEP decision. I need a meeting to review what happened.

special-ed.question: Teacher doesn't know my accommodations?
special-ed.explanation: All relevant staff must know your plan.
special-ed.script: My teacher doesn't seem to know about my 504 accommodations. The school is supposed to inform all my teachers. Can the 504 coordinator fix this?

special-ed.question: Suspended for disability-related behavior?
special-ed.short_answer: After 10 days, school must check if behavior is disability-related.
special-ed.script: I'm being suspended for behavior that's directly related to my disability. I believe a manifestation determination is required before discipline can continue.

special-ed.question: Testing accommodations for SAT/ACT?
special-ed.short_answer: Available if documented. Apply through testing organization.
special-ed.explanation: Each testing company has its own process.
special-ed.script: I need testing accommodations for the SAT or ACT. How do I apply through the testing organization, and what documentation do I need from the school?

special-ed.question: What happens when I turn 18/age out?
special-ed.short_answer: Services end at graduation or age 21-22 by state.
special-ed.explanation: Transition planning should start by age 16.
special-ed.script: I'm getting close to aging out of special education services. I want to understand my transition plan and what services I'm entitled to before that happens.

safety.question: Report unsafe conditions?
safety.short_answer: Tell admin, parent, or report to district.
safety.script: I want to report a safety issue. Something in the school isn't safe and I think it needs to be addressed before someone gets hurt.

safety.question: Can they give me medicine?
safety.short_answer: Only with parent permission and proper forms.
safety.script: I have a medical condition that requires medication, and I need you to get my parent's permission before giving me anything. Here are the forms my doctor filled out.

safety.question: Someone has a weapon?
safety.short_answer: Tell an adult IMMEDIATELY.
safety.script: I need to tell you something important right away. I'm concerned about a safety threat and someone needs to know about this immediately.

safety.question: Feeling unsafe at school?
safety.short_answer: Tell counselor, parent, or trusted adult.
safety.script: I don't feel safe at school right now and I need help. Can I please talk to the counselor or someone who can help me figure out a safety plan?

safety.question: Active shooter drills traumatizing me?
safety.short_answer: Talk to counselor. Some states limit realistic drills.
safety.explanation: Your mental health matters during safety exercises.
safety.script: The active shooter drills are really affecting my mental health. I want to participate in safety planning, but I need to talk to the counselor about how these drills are making me feel.

safety.question: Being threatened by another student?
safety.short_answer: Report immediately. Schools must protect you.
safety.explanation: Threats must be investigated and addressed.
safety.script: Another student has been threatening me and I have evidence. I need this taken seriously because I don't feel safe coming to school. The school is required to protect me.

safety.question: Severe allergy - school unprepared?
safety.short_answer: Schools must have emergency plans for known allergies.
safety.explanation: Federal law requires accommodations for disabilities including allergies.
safety.script: I have a severe allergy and I need to make sure there's an emergency action plan on file. My doctor has provided the necessary documentation.

safety.question: Mold or asbestos in school?
safety.short_answer: Report to admin and parents. Contact health department.
safety.explanation: Environmental hazards are serious and must be addressed.
safety.script: I've noticed what looks like mold or an environmental hazard in the building. I'm reporting this because it could be a health risk for students and staff.

safety.question: Sick but told I must come to school?
safety.short_answer: You can't be forced to attend when genuinely ill.
safety.script: I'm genuinely sick and I shouldn't be here. It's not safe for me or other students. I need to go home and I'll bring documentation when I return.

safety.question: Teacher denying bathroom all period?
safety.short_answer: Excessive restriction can cause health issues. Report if persistent.
safety.script: I have a legitimate health need to use the bathroom and I can't wait. Denying me access is affecting my health, and I have a doctor's note if needed.

technology.question: School see everything on school device?
technology.script: I understand that this is a school device and I have no expectation of privacy on it. I'll make sure to only use it for schoolwork.

technology.question: Track me at home?
technology.short_answer: If using school device or logged in, probably yes.
technology.script: I'm going to make sure I log out of the school device when I get home. I understand it can be monitored even outside of school hours.

technology.question: Blocked website I need?
technology.short_answer: Ask teacher or tech support to unblock for education.
technology.script: I need access to a specific website for a school project but it's blocked. Can you or my teacher request that it be unblocked for educational purposes?

technology.question: Accused of hacking?
technology.short_answer: Serious accusation. Get parents and maybe lawyer.
technology.script: I'm being accused of hacking, which is a serious accusation. I want my parents here before I answer any questions, and I may need to speak with a lawyer.

technology.question: Can they look at my personal phone screen?
technology.short_answer: Personal phones have more privacy protection than school devices.
technology.explanation: Your phone is your property. They need specific suspicion.
technology.script: This is my personal phone that I paid for. It's not a school device, and I don't think you can look through it without a very good reason and my parents' involvement.

technology.question: School WiFi sees what I browse?
technology.short_answer: Yes - on their network they can monitor traffic.
technology.explanation: Use your own mobile data for anything personal.
technology.script: I know the school can see what I browse on their WiFi, so I'll use my own mobile data for anything personal. I just want to keep my private stuff private.

technology.question: Online proctoring software too invasive?
technology.short_answer: Controversial and some schools are limiting it.
technology.explanation: Room scanning and webcam monitoring raises privacy concerns.
technology.script: I'm uncomfortable with how much this proctoring software accesses on my computer. Can you tell me exactly what it monitors and records? I want to know my privacy boundaries.

technology.question: AI detector says I cheated but I didn't?
technology.short_answer: AI detectors are unreliable. You can appeal with evidence.
technology.explanation: These tools have high false positive rates, especially for non-native speakers.
technology.script: I wrote this paper myself and I can prove it. AI detection tools have a high false positive rate. I have my drafts, notes, and revision history to show my writing process.

technology.question: School wants to install app on MY phone?
technology.short_answer: Cannot force software on personal devices.
technology.script: I'm not comfortable installing school monitoring software on my personal phone. That's my private property. Can the school provide a device instead?

technology.question: Admin reading school email?
technology.short_answer: Yes. School email is school property. No privacy there.
technology.explanation: Never use school email for personal conversations.
technology.script: I understand my school email isn't private and the school can read it. I'll use my personal email for anything that's not school-related.
next_steps: Use personal email for personal stuff

pay.question: Am I getting minimum wage?
pay.short_answer: Check your state - might be higher than federal $7.25.
pay.script: Hi, I want to make sure I'm being paid correctly. Can you tell me my exact hourly rate? I want to check that it meets our state's minimum wage requirement.

pay.question: Working off the clock?
pay.short_answer: Illegal if you're hourly. All work time must be paid.
pay.script: I've been asked to do work before clocking in and after clocking out. I want to make sure all my working time is being tracked and paid for, because that's the law.

pay.question: When's overtime?
pay.script: I've been working more than 40 hours this week. I want to confirm that I'll be getting overtime pay at time-and-a-half for those extra hours.

pay.question: Deductions from paycheck?
pay.short_answer: Only taxes and stuff you agreed to in writing.
pay.script: I noticed a deduction on my paycheck that I didn't authorize. Can you explain what it's for? I don't think you can deduct things without my written consent.

pay.question: Tips being taken?
pay.script: I want to understand how tips are being distributed here. I've heard that managers aren't allowed to take a share of employee tips, and I want to make sure that's not happening.

pay.question: Paycheck bounced?
pay.short_answer: Illegal. They owe you plus penalties.
pay.script: My paycheck didn't go through, and I need to be paid for the work I've already done. When can I expect to receive my wages?

pay.question: Paid less than coworkers?
pay.script: I've found out that coworkers doing the same job are being paid more than me. If the difference is based on my gender, race, or another protected characteristic, that's not legal.

pay.question: Commission not paid?
pay.short_answer: Must pay earned commission per agreement.
pay.script: I earned commission on those sales based on our agreement, and I haven't been paid for them yet. Can you show me the commission calculation?

pay.question: Training time - do they pay for it?
pay.short_answer: If training is required, it must be paid.
pay.explanation: Required training counts as work time.
pay.script: This training session was required by the company, so I need to be compensated for the time I spent there. Required training has to be paid.

pay.question: Uniform costs taken from pay?
pay.short_answer: Can't deduct below minimum wage. Some states ban uniform deductions.
pay.script: I understand I need a uniform, but these deductions are bringing my pay below minimum wage. I don't think that's allowed under the law.

hours.question: Do I get breaks?
hours.short_answer: Depends on state. Many require meal and rest breaks.
hours.explanation: Federal doesn't require, states often do.
hours.script: I've been working for several hours without a break. Can you tell me what the break policy is? I believe our state requires meal and rest breaks.

hours.question: Last minute schedule change?
hours.short_answer: Usually legal unless you have predictive scheduling laws.
hours.script: My schedule was changed at the last minute and it's causing real problems for me. Is there a policy about how much notice is required for schedule changes?

hours.question: Refuse overtime?
hours.short_answer: Usually they can require it, but must pay you.
hours.script: I understand overtime might be required, but I need to make sure I'm being paid the proper overtime rate for every extra hour I work.

hours.question: Stay late without pay?
hours.short_answer: All time worked must be paid.
hours.explanation: If required to stay, it's work time.
hours.script: I'm being asked to stay late but I was told to clock out first. I can't work off the clock — all time I'm required to be here needs to be paid.

hours.question: Hours as a minor?
hours.short_answer: Limited by law. Usually 3 hrs on school days.
hours.script: I'm under 18, and I think the hours I'm being scheduled might exceed what's legal for someone my age. Can we check the state rules for minor work hours?

hours.question: Scheduled during school?
hours.short_answer: Can't work during required school hours.
hours.script: I can't work during school hours — that's not allowed for workers my age. Here's my school schedule so we can make sure my shifts don't conflict.

hours.question: Clocking out but still working?
hours.short_answer: Illegal. All time working must be paid.
hours.script: I've been asked to do tasks after clocking out. Every minute I'm working needs to be on the clock. It's illegal to have me work for free.

hours.question: Split shifts - any extra pay?
hours.explanation: Check your state's rules on split shifts.
hours.script: I'm working a split shift today. Does our state require any additional pay or a premium for split shifts? I want to make sure I'm being compensated properly.

hours.question: Working through lunch unpaid?
hours.short_answer: If you can't leave freely during break, it's work time.
hours.script: I wasn't able to take a real break during my shift because I kept getting interrupted. If I can't freely leave during my break, that time should be paid.

hours.question: Opening/closing duties outside schedule?
hours.short_answer: Must be paid for all time you're required to be there.
hours.script: I'm spending time on opening and closing duties that aren't in my scheduled hours. I need to be paid for all the time I'm required to be here.

safety.question: Unsafe workplace?
safety.short_answer: Report it. OSHA complaints can be anonymous.
safety.explanation: You have right to safe work.
safety.script: I've noticed a safety issue at work and I need to report it. I want to make sure this is addressed before someone gets hurt. I know I can also file an anonymous OSHA complaint.

safety.question: Hurt at work?
safety.short_answer: Report immediately. Workers' comp covers you.
safety.script: I got hurt while I was working and I need to report it right away. I understand workers' compensation should cover my medical expenses. Where do I start?

safety.question: Who pays for safety gear?
safety.short_answer: Employer must provide it free.
safety.script: I need proper safety equipment to do this job safely. I believe the employer is required to provide that at no cost to me.

safety.question: Refuse dangerous work?
safety.short_answer: Only if immediate serious danger.
safety.script: I don't feel safe doing this particular task because it seems immediately dangerous. I have the right to refuse work that poses a serious threat to my safety.

safety.question: No training for dangerous equipment?
safety.short_answer: Employer must provide safety training. Report if missing.
safety.explanation: OSHA requires training before hazardous work.
safety.script: I haven't received any training on this equipment. I don't think I should operate it until I've been properly trained, which is an OSHA requirement.

safety.question: Exposed to chemicals without protection?
safety.short_answer: Employer must provide PPE and safety data sheets.
safety.explanation: Right to know about chemicals you work with.
safety.script: I'm being exposed to chemicals without proper protective equipment or information. I have the right to see the safety data sheets and have proper PPE provided.

safety.question: Coworker doing drugs on the job?
safety.short_answer: Report if it creates safety hazard.
safety.script: I need to report a safety concern about a coworker who seems impaired on the job. This is creating a dangerous situation for everyone.

safety.question: Extreme heat/cold at work?
safety.short_answer: OSHA requires reasonable working temperatures.
safety.script: The temperature in here is unsafe for working. Extreme heat or cold conditions are workplace safety hazards that need to be addressed.

safety.question: Workers comp claim being denied?
safety.short_answer: You can appeal. Get a workers comp attorney.
safety.script: My workers' compensation claim was denied, but I believe I'm entitled to coverage. I'd like to understand the appeal process and my options.

safety.question: Fired for filing safety complaint?
safety.short_answer: Illegal retaliation. File whistleblower complaint.
safety.script: I believe I was fired because I reported a safety issue. Retaliating against employees for safety complaints is illegal under OSHA protections.

harassment.question: Sexual harassment?
harassment.short_answer: Unwanted sexual conduct is illegal.
harassment.script: I need to report sexual harassment that's been happening at work. I have details about what occurred, when, and who was involved. This needs to be investigated.

harassment.question: Treated differently because of who I am?
harassment.short_answer: Discrimination based on protected traits is illegal.
harassment.script: I'm being treated differently than my coworkers because of who I am, and I believe that's discrimination. I've been keeping notes about what's been happening.

harassment.question: Punished for reporting?
harassment.short_answer: Retaliation is illegal.
harassment.script: Since I reported the harassment, things have gotten worse for me at work. I think I'm being retaliated against, which is illegal on its own.

harassment.question: HR not helping?
harassment.short_answer: File with EEOC.
harassment.script: I've tried reporting this through HR but nothing is happening. I'd like information about how to file a complaint with the EEOC because I need this addressed.

harassment.question: Inappropriate jokes making me uncomfortable?
harassment.short_answer: If severe or pervasive enough, it's harassment.
harassment.explanation: Doesn't have to be directed at you to be harassment.
harassment.script: The constant inappropriate jokes and comments are making it impossible to do my job. This has created a hostile work environment and I'm putting this complaint in writing.

harassment.question: Customer harassing me - boss won't help?
harassment.short_answer: Employer must protect you from third-party harassment too.
harassment.explanation: Doesn't matter if harasser is customer.
harassment.script: A customer has been harassing me and my manager won't do anything about it. My employer has a responsibility to protect me from harassment, even from customers.

harassment.question: Manager asking me on dates?
harassment.short_answer: Unwanted advances from a supervisor = sexual harassment.
harassment.explanation: Power dynamic makes this especially serious.
harassment.script: My manager keeps asking me out and making unwanted advances. I've said no and I need it to stop. I'm going to report this to HR because this is sexual harassment.

harassment.question: Afraid of retaliation if I report?
harassment.short_answer: Retaliation is illegal and separately punishable.
harassment.script: I want to report harassment, but I'm worried about retaliation. I want to document this conversation and make clear that anti-retaliation laws protect me.

harassment.question: Racist comments from coworker?
harassment.short_answer: Racial harassment is illegal. Report it.
harassment.explanation: Doesn't have to be slurs - pattern of comments counts.
harassment.script: A coworker keeps making racist comments around me. I've been documenting each incident and I'm formally reporting this as racial harassment.

harassment.question: Bullied at work - is that harassment?
harassment.short_answer: If based on protected trait (race, sex, etc.) yes. General bullying less protected.
harassment.script: I'm being bullied at work. While I'm documenting what's happening, I want to know if this is based on a protected characteristic because that would make it illegal harassment.

firing.question: Fired for no reason?
firing.script: I'd like to get the reason for my termination in writing. I want to understand exactly why I'm being let go so I can decide if this was done properly.

firing.question: Final paycheck?
firing.short_answer: Depends on state. Some say immediately.
firing.script: Now that I've been let go, when will I receive my final paycheck? I know our state has specific deadlines for how quickly final wages must be paid.

firing.question: Unemployment?
firing.short_answer: Usually yes if fired (not for misconduct).
firing.script: I was fired, and I'd like to apply for unemployment benefits right away. Can you confirm that I wasn't terminated for misconduct so I know where I stand?

firing.question: Two weeks notice required?
firing.script: I'm giving my notice and my last day will be on this date. I want to make sure I receive all my remaining pay and any accrued benefits.

firing.question: Sign something when leaving?
firing.short_answer: Read carefully. Might give up rights.
firing.script: I've been asked to sign a separation agreement, but I need time to read through it carefully. I'd like to take it home and possibly have a lawyer review it before I sign anything.

firing.question: Fired while on medical leave?
firing.short_answer: May be illegal if FMLA applies or it's retaliation.
firing.script: I was on approved medical leave when I was terminated. I believe firing someone who's on protected leave is illegal, and I'd like this decision reviewed.

firing.question: Fired for something everyone does?
firing.short_answer: If selectively enforced based on who you are, that's discrimination.
firing.script: I was fired for something that other employees do regularly without consequences. If I'm being singled out because of who I am, that's discrimination.

firing.question: Can they make me train my replacement?
firing.short_answer: Can ask but you're not obligated after termination notice.
firing.explanation: Once fired, you owe nothing extra.
firing.script: I understand you want me to train my replacement, but I was just told I'm being let go. I'm not obligated to do that, and I'd rather focus on my transition.

firing.question: Written up unfairly - what to do?
firing.short_answer: You can usually write a rebuttal for your file.
firing.explanation: Ask to add your response to the write-up.
firing.script: I disagree with this write-up and I'd like to add my own written response to be included in my personnel file. That's my right.

firing.question: Constructive dismissal - what is it?
firing.short_answer: When conditions are so bad you're forced to quit. May still be 'fired.'
firing.explanation: Making work unbearable to force you out.
firing.script: The working conditions here have been made deliberately unbearable, and I feel forced to quit. I want to document that this feels like constructive dismissal.

privacy.question: Read my work emails?
privacy.short_answer: Yes. Work email = work property.
privacy.script: I understand the company may monitor work email, but I want to be clear about the policy. Can you show me the written monitoring policy so I know what's being tracked?

privacy.question: Drug test me?
privacy.short_answer: Often yes, especially for hiring.
privacy.script: I understand drug testing may be part of the job. Before I take any test, I'd like to see the written policy about when testing happens and what my rights are.

privacy.question: Fired for social media?
privacy.short_answer: Often yes. But discussing work conditions is protected.
privacy.script: I was fired over something I posted on social media during my own time. Was this really a fireable offense? I'd like to understand the specific policy I allegedly violated.

privacy.question: Boss checking my personal phone?
privacy.short_answer: Cannot search personal devices without consent.
privacy.script: That's my personal phone that I own. I don't believe you have the right to look through it. Company policies apply to company devices, not my personal property.

privacy.question: GPS tracking in work vehicle?
privacy.short_answer: Usually legal in company vehicles during work hours.
privacy.script: I understand this is a company vehicle and it may be tracked during work hours. But I want to know — is it also being tracked when I'm off the clock?

privacy.question: Cameras in the breakroom?
privacy.short_answer: Legal in common areas. NOT in bathrooms or changing areas.
privacy.explanation: Reasonable expectation of privacy in some areas.
privacy.script: I noticed cameras in the break room. I want to make sure there are no cameras in the bathrooms or changing areas, because that would be illegal.

privacy.question: Background check found old record?
privacy.short_answer: Depends on state laws about what can be reported/considered.
privacy.explanation: Many states limit how far back checks can go.
privacy.script: I understand a background check is part of the process. But I want to know what can legally be reported in our state. Some records may be too old to include.

privacy.question: Medical info shared with coworkers?
privacy.short_answer: Generally illegal. Medical info must be kept confidential.
privacy.explanation: ADA limits disclosure of medical information.
privacy.script: My medical information was shared with other employees without my permission. That's a violation of my privacy rights under the ADA, and I'd like this addressed immediately.

privacy.question: Employer asking about my religion?
privacy.short_answer: Can't ask in hiring. Must accommodate unless undue hardship.
privacy.explanation: Religious inquiries in hiring are illegal.
privacy.script: I don't believe you can ask me about my religious beliefs during the hiring process. That's not a legally permitted interview question.

privacy.question: Forced to share social media passwords?
privacy.short_answer: Many states ban requiring social media passwords for employment.
privacy.explanation: Growing number of states protect this.
privacy.script: I don't think you can require me to hand over my personal social media passwords. A growing number of states have laws specifically prohibiting this.

minors.question: What jobs can I do as a teen?
minors.short_answer: Depends on age. Some jobs banned for under 18.
minors.explanation: Hazardous work restricted.
minors.script: I'm under 18, and I think the hours you're scheduling me might not be legal for someone my age. Can we look at the state rules together?

minors.question: Work late on school night?
minors.short_answer: Limited hours during school week.
minors.explanation: Usually can't work past certain time.
minors.script: I know that workers my age need a work permit. Can you help me understand the process for getting the right paperwork?

minors.question: Work permit needed?
minors.short_answer: Many states require work permits for minors.
minors.explanation: Get from school usually.
minors.script: This task seems like it might be on the restricted list for workers under 18. I want to make sure I'm not being asked to do something that's not legal for my age.

minors.question: Boss making me do dangerous stuff?
minors.short_answer: Minors have extra protections from hazardous work.
minors.explanation: Some tasks banned for minors.
minors.script: I'm not old enough to work unsupervised during these hours. I think having a minor work alone at night might violate state labor laws.

minors.question: Working past midnight as a minor?
minors.short_answer: Illegal on school nights in most states. Limited on non-school nights.
minors.explanation: Strict hour limits for workers under 18.
minors.script: I can't work past the legal cutoff time for someone my age, especially on a school night. I need my schedule adjusted to follow the law.

minors.question: Using a slicer/fryer under 18?
minors.short_answer: Many food equipment banned for minors under federal law.
minors.explanation: Hazardous equipment restricted for under-18.
minors.script: I don't think I'm legally allowed to operate this equipment at my age. Federal law restricts certain machines for workers under 18.

minors.question: Serving alcohol as a minor?
minors.short_answer: State laws vary. Many allow serving at 18 but not 16.
minors.explanation: Alcohol laws are state-specific.
minors.script: I need to check the legal age for serving alcohol in our state. I want to make sure I'm not being asked to do something I'm not old enough to do.

minors.question: Boss making me work alone at night?
minors.short_answer: Many states prohibit minors working alone, especially at night.
minors.explanation: Safety concerns for young workers are taken seriously.
minors.script: I'm uncomfortable being scheduled to work alone, especially at night. I think there are rules about minors working without supervision.

minors.question: Internship but doing real work unpaid?
minors.short_answer: If you're doing productive work, you likely must be paid.
minors.explanation: Unpaid internships have strict rules about who benefits.
minors.script: I'm doing actual productive work here, not just learning. If I'm contributing to the business, I think I should be getting paid for my time.

minors.question: Can parents take my earnings?
minors.short_answer: Complex - depends on state. Generally your money is yours.
minors.explanation: Some states protect minor's earnings from parents.
minors.script: The money I earned from this job is mine. I want to understand my rights about my own earnings and how to protect them.

scheduling.question: On call without pay?
scheduling.short_answer: If you must stay available, you might need to be paid.
scheduling.script: My schedule keeps changing at the last minute and it's really hard to plan my life around it. Does our area have any fair scheduling laws I should know about?

scheduling.question: Shift cancelled last minute?
scheduling.short_answer: Some places have 'show up pay' laws.
scheduling.script: I was told I have to stay late or come in on my day off. I want to understand whether I'm actually required to do that, or if I can say no.

scheduling.question: Too many hours?
scheduling.short_answer: No federal cap but must be paid. Minors have limits.
scheduling.script: I was called in for a shift that was cancelled when I arrived. I want to know if I'm entitled to any pay for showing up as scheduled.

scheduling.question: Need day off they won't give?
scheduling.short_answer: No law requires time off except FMLA for family/medical.
scheduling.script: The schedule just changed again with almost no notice. I've already made plans based on what was posted. Is there a minimum notice requirement?

scheduling.question: Predictive scheduling - any protections?
scheduling.short_answer: Some cities/states require advance schedule posting.
scheduling.script: I'd like to know when the schedule is supposed to be posted. Some places have laws requiring advance schedule notice.

scheduling.question: Called in early - do I have to come?
scheduling.short_answer: Usually can't be forced outside agreed hours. But may affect standing.
scheduling.explanation: Not legally required but may have consequences.
scheduling.script: I can't come in on such short notice. I wasn't scheduled and I've made other commitments.

scheduling.question: No weekends off ever?
scheduling.short_answer: No federal right to weekends. Some state rules for retail.
scheduling.script: I've been working every weekend without a day off. Are there any laws about guaranteed days off or consecutive work limits?

scheduling.question: Religious day off denied?
scheduling.short_answer: Must accommodate religious observance unless undue hardship.
scheduling.script: I need this day off for religious observance. My employer is required to accommodate my religious practices unless it would cause real hardship.

scheduling.question: Double shift with no break between?
scheduling.short_answer: Some states require minimum hours between shifts.
scheduling.script: I'm being scheduled for a double shift with barely any time between them. I want to check if there's a minimum rest requirement in our state.

scheduling.question: Schedule conflict with school?
scheduling.short_answer: For minors, school takes priority by law.
scheduling.explanation: Can't schedule minors during school hours.
scheduling.script: I have school during those hours and I can't miss class for work. For someone my age, school has to come first — that's the law.

tips.question: Tip pooling?
tips.short_answer: Okay with other tipped workers. Managers usually can't take.
tips.script: I want to understand how the tip pool works here. Who gets included, and is management taking a share? Because managers aren't allowed to take our tips.

tips.question: Credit card tips?
tips.short_answer: Must give you full tip amount. Small processing fee sometimes okay.
tips.script: I'm working in a position that earns tips, but I'm being paid below regular minimum wage. If my tips don't make up the difference, my employer has to cover it.

tips.question: Making less than minimum with tips?
tips.short_answer: Employer must make up difference to minimum wage.
tips.script: Can you explain how the credit card tips are being distributed? I want to make sure we're getting the full amount that customers intended for us.

tips.question: Tip out to kitchen staff?
tips.short_answer: Legal if employer pays full minimum. Rules vary.
tips.script: I want to understand the tip-out policy. I know the rules changed recently about who can be included in tip pools, so I want to make sure it's legal.

tips.question: Automatic gratuity - is that my tip?
tips.short_answer: IRS treats auto-grat as service charge, not tip. Goes to employer first.
tips.script: That automatic gratuity is being treated as a service charge, not a tip. I want to know how it's being distributed because the rules are different.

tips.question: Boss takes cut of delivery tips?
tips.short_answer: Managers cannot take employee tips. Period.
tips.script: My boss is taking a cut of our delivery tips, and that's not legal. Tips belong to the employees who earn them, not management.

tips.question: Paying for customer walkouts from tips?
tips.short_answer: Can't make you pay for dine-and-dash if it drops you below minimum.
tips.script: I'm being asked to pay for a customer who walked out on their bill, and it's coming from my tips. That would drop me below minimum wage, which isn't allowed.

tips.question: Cash tips - do I have to report them?
tips.short_answer: Legally yes for taxes. Practically, track them.
tips.script: I want to make sure I'm tracking my cash tips correctly for tax purposes. Can you help me understand the proper way to report them?

tips.question: Digital tip options not offered to customers?
tips.short_answer: If employer controls tip options, they must pass tips to you.
tips.explanation: All tips from customers belong to workers.
tips.script: I think we should offer digital tipping options for customers. Whatever tips come in need to be passed along to us, the workers.

tips.question: Tip credit - what is it?
tips.short_answer: Employer pays less hourly expecting tips to cover minimum. Must make up difference.
tips.explanation: If tips don't reach minimum, employer pays the gap.
tips.script: I want to make sure my total earnings — tip credit wage plus actual tips — add up to at least minimum wage. If they don't, my employer has to make up the difference.

contracts.question: Non-compete agreement?
contracts.short_answer: Many states limit or ban them, especially for low-wage workers.
contracts.script: I was told there's a non-compete agreement I need to sign. Before I do, I want to understand exactly what it restricts and whether it's enforceable in our state.

contracts.question: Signed something I didn't understand?
contracts.short_answer: You're usually bound. Get lawyer to review.
contracts.script: I don't fully understand these contract terms and I'm not comfortable signing anything right now. I'd like to take this home and possibly have someone review it first.

contracts.question: Job different than promised?
contracts.short_answer: Verbal promises hard to enforce. Check written agreement.
contracts.script: I was told I can only bring disputes to an arbitration panel, not a court. I want to understand what I'm giving up by agreeing to that.

contracts.question: Forced to sign non-disclosure?
contracts.short_answer: Can't prevent you from reporting illegal activity.
contracts.explanation: NDAs can't cover up law violations.
contracts.script: This non-disclosure agreement seems very broad. I want to be clear — this can't prevent me from reporting illegal activity or safety violations, right?

contracts.question: Arbitration clause - what does it mean?
contracts.short_answer: Means disputes go to private arbitrator instead of court.
contracts.explanation: Usually favors employer but sometimes required.
contracts.script: I see there's an arbitration clause in this agreement. Can you explain exactly what disputes this covers and what my options are?

contracts.question: Contract says I owe training costs if I quit?
contracts.short_answer: Training repayment agreements vary in enforceability.
contracts.explanation: Some states limit these. May not be enforceable.
contracts.script: The contract says I'd owe money for training if I leave early. I want to check whether that kind of repayment clause is actually enforceable in our state.

contracts.question: Didn't get promised raise in writing?
contracts.short_answer: Verbal promises hard to enforce. Get everything in writing.
contracts.script: I was promised a raise verbally, but it hasn't happened. Going forward, I'd like to get any compensation promises in writing so we're both on the same page.

contracts.question: At-will vs contract - difference?
contracts.short_answer: At-will = fired anytime. Contract = specific terms and protections.
contracts.explanation: Most US workers are at-will unless they have a contract.
contracts.script: Am I an at-will employee or do I have a contract? That makes a big difference for my rights, and I want to be clear on my status.

contracts.question: Independent contractor but treated like employee?
contracts.short_answer: Misclassification is illegal. You may be owed benefits.
contracts.explanation: If they control when/how you work, you're probably an employee.
contracts.script: I'm classified as an independent contractor, but I'm being treated exactly like an employee — set schedule, required to be on-site, using company tools. I think I may be misclassified.

contracts.question: Signed something under pressure?
contracts.short_answer: Contracts signed under duress may be voidable.
contracts.script: I felt pressured to sign this agreement quickly and I don't think I fully understood what I was agreeing to. I'd like to discuss whether this is still binding.
